_meta.role: Master Thesis Proposal: TinyML for Predictive Maintenance in Embedded Systems

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, working where embedded systems and machine learning meet. I write bare-metal embedded C for microcontrollers with timer-synchronized data acquisition and interrupt-driven sensor capture, and build the model-optimization side too: quantization-aware training with integer-only inference and measured accuracy, memory, and latency trade-offs.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, turning 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a tap-detection algorithm on the raw accelerometer stream using z-axis differential thresholding, with software calibration to reject jitter.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Curated and annotated a labeled classification dataset, then trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 images to 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation.
Exported the trained model to ONNX and TFLite for resource-constrained on-device deployment.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a PyQt and Matplotlib GUI for real-time laboratory data acquisition and experimental visualization; version-controlled in GitLab.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Quantization-Aware Training for Integer-Only Inference
bullets: Implemented quantization-aware training in PyTorch with straight-through-estimator fake quantization, int8 symmetric weights, and uint8 activations; integer-only inference reaches 97.43% on the MNIST test set.
Calibrated the activation scale with an EMA observer and folded it into a fixed-point requantization multiplier and shift; exported int8 weights and golden test vectors.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller firmware in bare-metal embedded C at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM, holding a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a register-level I2C driver for synchronized sensor data acquisition.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for task coordination on an STM32 microcontroller, driving multi-servo PWM motor control from interrupt-driven UART commands.
Ran YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson for real-time tracking, streaming commands to the microcontroller over UART; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop - Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
